sections.h2: What paperwork must a Virginia landlord give a new tenant?
sections.html:
A landlord must offer a written rental agreement and hand over the statement of tenant rights and responsibilities from the Department of Housing and Community Development. That duty is in Va. Code 55.1-1204.

Both sides sign an acknowledgment form showing the tenant received the statement. If the tenant will not sign, the landlord records the date or dates the form was provided and that the tenant did not sign. The landlord then gives the tenant a copy of the signed agreement and the statement within 10 business days of the effective date.

Missing that delivery does not void the lease. It does stop the landlord from filing or keeping any action, including an unlawful detainer, for an alleged lease violation until the tenant has received the statement. For an owner selling a rented house, a missing acknowledgment is the first thing to look for in the file.

sections.h2: What if there is no written lease?
sections.html:
If the landlord never offers a written agreement, the same section creates a tenancy by operation of law with fixed terms. A buyer or seller who finds an oral arrangement should know these defaults.

  • The chapter applies to the unit, and the term is 12 months with no automatic renewal, except for month-to-month cases.
  • Rent is paid in 12 equal installments at an agreed amount, or at fair market rent if none was agreed.
  • Rent is due the first of the month and counts as late after the fifth.
  • The landlord may collect a deposit of up to two months of rent.
  • The parties may sign a written agreement at any time during the 12 months.

Where a rent period is weekly, the tenancy is week-to-week. In all other cases it is month-to-month unless the agreement says otherwise.

sections.h2: How much can a landlord charge for late rent and payment fees?
sections.html:
A late charge is allowed only if the written agreement provides for it, and it cannot exceed the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic rent or 10 percent of the balance due.

A landlord must accept rent and deposit by check and money order, and give a written receipt for cash or money order payments. Collection or processing fees are barred unless an alternative with no extra fee is offered. Where a fee is charged, it cannot exceed the actual out-of-pocket cost billed by a third party for the card or electronic payment. Landlords with four or fewer rental units are not required to accept debit or credit cards.

A tenant can ask in writing for a statement of charges and payments, and the landlord must provide it within 10 business days, covering the tenancy or the past 12 months, whichever is shorter.

sections.h2: What extra rules apply to landlords with more than four rentals?
sections.html:
Landlords who own more than four rental units, or more than a 10 percent interest in more than four, must follow added notice rules for renewals. Those rules sit in subsection K of 55.1-1204 and are summarized below.

RuleVersion now in forceVersion effective July 1, 2027
Rent increase noticeWritten notice at least 60 days before the term endsWritten notice at least 90 days before the term ends, with a reply deadline at least 30 days after delivery
Nonrenewal noticeAt least 60 days before the term endsAt least 60 days before the term ends
Payment plan for small rent balancesNot requiredRequired before the 14-day rent notice in certain cases (55.1-1245)

Neither notice rule applies to a periodic tenancy created by operation of law under subsection C of 55.1-1253. If you rent out one house, these provisions probably do not reach you, but a portfolio owner selling several houses should treat them as live.

sections.h2: How does the security deposit work?
sections.html:
A Virginia landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit above two months of periodic rent, and must itemize any deductions in writing within 45 days after the tenancy ends or the tenant leaves, whichever is last. The rules are in Va. Code 55.1-1226.

  • Deductions are limited to accrued rent and late charges, damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, other charges in the lease, and actual damages for breach.
  • With more than one tenant, the refund is one check payable to all of them, unless they agreed otherwise in writing.
  • If no forwarding address is given, the landlord may hold the money, and after one year past the 45 days may send it to the State Treasurer as unclaimed property.
  • A landlord may withhold a reasonable part for unpaid water, sewer or other utility bills if prior written notice was given; a tenant who proves payment gets the money back.
  • Records of deductions must be kept for two years and be open to the tenant during business hours.
  • A tenant may be offered damage insurance in place of a deposit if it meets the listed criteria.

Tenants can ask to be present at the move-out inspection, which must happen within 72 hours of delivering possession. If the landlord willfully fails to comply, the court orders the deposit returned along with actual damages and reasonable attorney fees, unless the tenant owes rent, in which case the deposit is credited against that rent.

sections.h2: What happens to the deposit when the rental is sold?
sections.html:
The person who holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends is bound by the deposit statute and must return any deposit that is duly owed. That is true however the interest was acquired, whether or not the deposit was transferred, and regardless of any contract between the old and new owners.

For a seller, the practical steps are simple.

  • List every deposit held and who paid it.
  • Collect the itemized deduction records for the last two years.
  • Ask the buyer to agree in writing how deposits will be credited at closing, and confirm the tenant is told.
  • Keep the signed rights acknowledgment and the lease together for the buyer.

These steps are suggestions for organizing the file. They are not legal advice, and an attorney should review the closing paperwork.

sections.h2: What remedies does a landlord have after ending the lease?
sections.html:
Once the lease is terminated, 55.1-1251 gives the landlord a claim for possession and rent, plus a separate claim for actual damages, attorney fees and service costs. Damages can include rent through the end of the term or the start of a new tenancy, but the landlord must mitigate and cannot seek accelerated rent in a post-possession judgment.

When a tenant moves out by choice or by writ, the deposit is credited following the 45-day rule above.

Local rental registration, inspection programs and short-term rental rules vary by city and county. We did not confirm any of them from an official local page, so ask the local housing or zoning office before you rent or sell a unit.

faqs.q: What is the maximum security deposit in Virginia?
faqs.a: Two months of periodic rent. The landlord must itemize deductions and return the balance within 45 days after the tenancy ends or the tenant leaves, whichever is last.

faqs.q: Can a landlord charge any late fee in Virginia?
faqs.a: Only if the written lease provides for it, and the charge cannot exceed the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic rent or 10 percent of the balance owed.

faqs.q: Does a missing tenant rights form void a lease?
faqs.a: No. The lease stays valid, but the landlord cannot file or maintain an unlawful detainer for an alleged lease violation until the tenant has the statement of rights and responsibilities.

faqs.q: What are the default terms if there is no written lease?
faqs.a: A 12-month tenancy with no automatic renewal, rent due on the first and late after the fifth, and a deposit of up to two months of rent. A weekly payer is week-to-week.

faqs.q: Who must return the tenant's deposit after a sale?
faqs.a: The holder of the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends. That holder is bound even if the deposit did not transfer with the property.

faqs.q: Do larger landlords have extra duties?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of more than four rental units must give written notice of rent increases and nonrenewal at least 60 days before the term ends, and the rules shift on July 1, 2027, to a 90-day notice for increases.
